speaker: Mr Vikram Nair
text: asked the Minister for Digital Development and Information in light of the US Court's finding that Meta and Alphabet were negligent in designing platforms that harmed young people, whether the Government will consider action to regulate young people's access to social media platforms, including a potential ban on such use.

speaker: The Minister of State for Digital Development and Information (Ms Rahayu Mahzam) (for the Minister for Digital Development and Information)
text: The answer given also addresses related questions for written answer by Mr Louis Chua and Miss Elysa Chen in today's Order Paper.

speaker: The Minister of State for Digital Development and Information (Ms Rahayu Mahzam) (for the Minister for Digital Development and Information)
text: The Member may wish to refer to the answer given.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
text: I just want to highlight that, indeed, we are taking reference from the judgment, from the decision, and the information that we are seeing, the findings, actually add to the growing body of evidence.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
text: We know that the harms are real and we are taking it seriously.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
text: So, it is not that we are not doing anything.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
text: We have been acting on protecting and safeguarding our young children from the harms online.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
text: But we take a different approach in that we also want something that is more effective.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
text: A more durable approach that will withstand the test of time and the test of evolution of the technologies.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
text: Because, as what the Member pointed out, what we have found from the decisions was that there were some specific features and dimensions of the social media platforms that actually impact the youths.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
text: So, it is not just about saying, "Okay, none at all".

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
text: Because if you just say, "Okay, do not use it at all", you may not even solve the problem.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
text: What we are trying to do is to look at what is it that is causing the harm.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
text: Our approach has always been one that is outcomes-driven.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
text: And we have been building progressively on this.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
text: We introduced age assurance for apps and we also have the annual reporting that the designated social media services have to provide to us.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
text: So, that shows that there is a mechanism for us to actually take action.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
text: We are going to understand it a bit better.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
text: These are the things that are actually causing the harms the direct messaging from strangers, auto-play, other features that drive excessive use, emerging risks from AI companions and all that.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
text: So, we are actually going to break it down and see how we can improve it.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
text: And if there is a need for stronger action, we will take it.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
text: But we are learning robustly from many different countries.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
text: Minister Desmond Lee made reference to Estonia, his visit to Estonia.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
text: Estonia is a country that we look up to, because it is quite advanced.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
text: And so, this idea of a blanket or social media ban is not a globally accepted position.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
text: Estonia has not applied it; in fact, I think Belgium as well as the state of New York.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
text: In fact, Australia has also amended its legislation to be a bit more targeted, looking at the design features.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
text: So, firstly, we are not starting on a blank slate.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
text: We do have safeguards in place and we do not think just rushing into having a ban may necessarily be the best thing.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
text: We are not foreclosing it as a decision, but we are studying what is more effective to achieve the desired outcome that you will want to see.
